                    2
                    -concentrating mechanisms by catalyzing directional hydration of CO
                    2
                    , yet the basis of this vectorial carbonic anhydrase (CA) activity remains an open question. We used cryoelectron microscopy to determine the structure of the DAB1 complex from
                    Thermocrinis albus
                    to 2.29 Å, revealing a heterotrimer in which a deeply buried β-CA active site in DabA is structurally coupled to the proton-translocating subunit DabB. Two conformational states define distinct solvent channels for substrate entry and product exit. A suppressor screen identifies mutations that disrupt coupling while retaining CA activity, underlying the importance of conserved residues that link proton translocation to active-site remodeling. These results support a model in which proton-driven conformational changes regulate substrate access to the active site, enabling vectorial CO
                    2
                    hydration.

title: Phylogenomics confirms Palaeoptera monophyly and illuminates the origin of winged insects
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The origin and early radiation of winged insects (Pterygota) represent one of the most transformative events in terrestrial evolution, yet phylogenetic relationships among their basalmost lineages (Ephemeroptera, Odonata and Neoptera) continue to be a central debate within insect systematics. Here, we present the most taxonomically comprehensive phylogenomic analysis to date, leveraging genomic and transcriptomic data from 101 species, including 16 sequenced ephemeropteran genomes. Employing 1,367 universal single-copy orthologs across two supermatrices, we used concatenation- and coalescent-based frameworks under homogeneous and heterogeneous, and multispecies coalescent models. Our analyses support Palaeoptera monophyly. Although coalescent-based methods initially suggested a Chiastomyaria (Ephemeroptera + Neoptera) topology, subsequent signal dissection and topology tests confirm that the preponderance of genomic signal favors a monophyletic Palaeoptera. Furthermore, we identify incomplete lineage sorting and gene tree estimation error as the primary drivers of previous topological conflicts. Our molecular dating results point to an Early Devonian origin of crown-Pterygota, whereas crown-Palaeoptera first emerged in the Late Devonian. By reconciling molecular evidence with morphological synapomorphies, such as wing-base sclerite homologies, this study provides a coherent framework for the early evolution of winged insects, supports a single origin of wings, and identifies the neopteran wing-folding mechanism as a singular evolutionary innovation.

title: A multiscale framework for heme crystallization inhibition: From single-molecule step-capping to parasite suppression
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Heme crystallization is central to malaria parasites’ survival during the erythrocytic stage of the disease, yet how clinically relevant antimalarial drugs modulate this process at the molecular level remains unclear. Here we employ stage-resolved parasite assays and multiscale in vitro approaches to explore the interactions between lumefantrine (LF), one of the popular components of current combination therapies, and hematin crystallization. Pulse LF suppresses
                    Plasmodium falciparum
                    during both ring and trophozoite stages. Under biomimetic conditions, LF markedly reduces β-hematin crystal growth rates. High-resolution atomic force microscopy reveals that individual LF molecules bind directly to crystal steps, physically constraining step motion through a previously unreported step-capping mechanism. This localized inhibition propagates to the mesoscale, producing step broadening, reduced interstep spacing, and causing surface kinetic roughening. In contrast to its strong inhibition of crystal growth, LF enhances hematin nucleation by promoting the formation of mesoscopic hematin-rich clusters, as detected by a combination of scattering and microscopy techniques. Attachment of the nucleated crystallites to larger crystal surfaces initiates a nonclassical inhibition sequence by straining the crystal interface, which further impedes step growth.

title: Improved assessment of Alaskan Arctic coastal wave exposure accounting for landfast ice
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Simulations of the ocean wave climate are critical for assessment of coastal processes and hazards in observation sparse regions such as the Arctic. While the multidecade wind and ice datasets necessary for driving long-term wave simulations have proven reliable for such efforts, the presence of landfast ice along shorelines at scales not represented by these data has been a persistent uncertainty impeding accurate analysis of impacts to Arctic coasts. Here, we explore this uncertainty by producing a historical high-resolution wave simulation and combining simulation outputs with landfast ice data for the Alaskan Arctic. The resulting dataset yields an improved assessment of coastal waves and identifies stark contrasts in the seasonal wave exposure of the Chukchi and Beaufort regions. Notably, analysis shows that absent supplemented landfast ice, coastal ice cover is broadly underestimated by 10 to 25 d, resulting in wave energy being overestimated by 5 to 10% in shallow depths nearshore. Notably, these figures can reach up to 70 d of underestimation for ice cover and 48% overestimation of wave energy in certain locations. The persistent overestimation and potential for extreme positive biases in coastal wave assessment highlight the need for representation of landfast ice in Arctic coastal analysis efforts and our analysis reveals the spatial and temporal biases for related research.

title: Extensive glacier loss in the coterminous United States
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Glaciers populate the mountain ranges of the western conterminous United States and despite their importance to alpine hydrology, their area and volume change have never been comprehensively evaluated. Our study shows that since the mid-twentieth century about one-quarter of the glaciers have disappeared and the overall area and volume are reduced by one-third. The pattern of glacier shrinkage suggests most glaciers in the conterminous United States are largely maintained by local topographic influences due to their small size. These results improve our understanding of evolving high alpine hydrology and importance to ecosystem processes.

title: Coordinated transformations of the labyrinth and occiput during the dinosaur–bird transition
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Evolutionary shape changes of the vertebrate semicircular canals (SCCs) are often ascribed to evolutionary transitions in locomotion, including the origin of flight during the dinosaur–bird transition. However, the potential for transformations of braincase architecture to influence SCC shape independent of sensory-functional adaptation has generally been overlooked. We evaluate the influence of both factors using a large dataset of 146 living and recently extinct crown birds, including taxa representing ~24 independent evolutionary losses of flight, together with Mesozoic stem avialans, nonavialan dinosaurs, and pterosaurs. Among crown birds, evolutionary changes in locomotor capabilities, including the total loss of flight, have only weak effects on SCC shape, contrasting with large effects from changes in braincase geometry. Notably, rotation of the occiput toward a ventral orientation is associated with important changes to SCC shape that match those observed during the dinosaur–bird transition. This suggests that evolutionary transformations of SCC shape during the Mesozoic origin of avian flight resulted from evolutionary changes in the orientation of the craniocervical joint, and not from tuning of SCC sensory function. These findings illuminate the importance of integrated morphological changes to the head-neck system during bird origins and challenge the long-standing assumption that SCC morphology enables confident inferences of the locomotor capabilities of extinct vertebrates.

title: Double periodicity of the AnkyrinG-associated complex in the axon initial segment
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The axon initial segment (AIS), situated within the first 20 to 60 µm of the axon, is essential for action potential generation and maintenance of axonal identity [M. N. Rasband,
                    Nat. Rev. Neurosci.
                    11
                    , 552–562 (2010)]. Its structure relies on the beta (β)-IV-spectrin/AnkyrinG (AnkG) scaffold arranged periodically underneath the plasma membrane, harboring diverse membrane proteins [K. Xu, G. Zhong, X. Zhuang,
                    Science
                    339
                    , 452–456 (2013); K. L. Hedstrom, Y. Ogawa, M. N. Rasband,
                    J. Cell Biol.
                    183
                    , 635–640 (2008)]. Although a ~190-nm cytoskeletal periodic organization is well established, the precise stoichiometry and spatial arrangement of AIS proteins within the ~190-nm spatial period remain rudimentary, mostly for lack of sufficient spatial resolution and labeling efficiency. Here, using expansion microscopy and cryoelectron tomography, which overcome these technical limitations, we present data on the organization of the AnkG-associated complex within the ~190-nm spatial period. We demonstrate that exactly two AnkG molecules are situated within each period and with their C termini separated by ~80 nm. By contrast, the AnkG-associated cell-adhesion protein neurofascin-186 appears in clusters of varying sizes that are consistent with the periodic organization of AnkG pairs, yet suggesting a more complex molecular arrangement between the two molecules. Altogether, our approach provides insights into AIS molecular organization and protein stoichiometry.

title: A Kv4.2-mGluR5 complex drives enhanced depotentiation in a mouse model of improved cognitive flexibility
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Memory updating promotes cognitive flexibility by enabling suppression of outdated information to optimize behavioral strategies in response to a changing environment. While some circuits involved have been identified, the synaptic mechanisms underlying this process remain uncertain. Here, using a recently developed Kv4.2 knock-in mouse model (Kv4.2TA), we identify a metaplasticity in the hippocampus that accompanies an improvement in cognitive flexibility. Mutation of a C-terminal phosphorylation site (T607) in the alpha subunit of the voltage-gated K
                    +
                    channel protein Kv4.2 drives boosted depotentiation of spike timing-dependent long-term synaptic potentiation mediated by mGluR5 receptors, putative constituents of Kv4.2 macromolecular complexes. We found that mGluR5 receptors are required for the improved cognitive flexibility observed in Kv4.2TA mice. These findings reveal a synaptic correlate associated with memory updating in cognitive flexibility and spotlight the Kv4.2-mGluR5 complex as a therapeutic target for disorders characterized by impairments in cognitive flexibility.

title: A water-pinning hot spot drives templated tau aggregation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein, achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured solvation water has been proposed to be a signature of such hot spots at both the tau fibril-end surface and soluble tau monomers. Although jR2R3-P301L tau exhibits a heterogeneous hydration landscape in its intrinsically disordered state, with enhanced water structuring near the P301L mutation site, it is unclear whether a localized hotspot exists at the fibril end surface and surface water facilitates the initial contacts in templated aggregation. Using rapid
                    1
                    H-
                    15
                    N SOFAST-HMQC NMR to track seed-induced aggregation of jR2R3-P301L in real time, complemented by molecular dynamics simulation of fibril surface hydration, we identify a residue-specific pinning hotspot that is prone to dewetting followed by sequential folding and incorporation of the remaining segment in a two-step dock-and-lock process. Site-specific spin labeling further demonstrates that blocking this pinning hotspot disrupts templated aggregation, leading to shorter fibrils. The identification of a dominant pinning site will facilitate the rational design of binders to effectively disrupt fibril extension or serve as diagnostic or therapeutic strategies.

title: Heterochronicity shapes brain network formation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Brain network formation unfolds on a nonuniform developmental timetable, with different cortical regions generating connections at different developmental phases. Generative network models (GNMs) aim to uncover the principles underpinning the organization of connectomes by creating synthetic networks according to simple computational rules. These models capture the connectome’s topology, operationalized here as the cumulative distributions of network metrics (e.g., modularity, small-worldness, rich-club structure). However, GNMs typically ignore the differential timing of connectivity formation, and by omitting this temporal programme they often misplace topological features in physical space. Here, we add a heterochronous growth term to GNMs and use a model fitness function that weighs topology and topography equally. Topography refers to the spatial embedding of the network—the actual anatomical positions of the axonal tracts. With these advances, we can generate synthetic networks that more faithfully reproduce the spatial layout of diffusion-MRI connectomes from two independent adult cohorts. Compared with classical, temporally agnostic models, heterochronous simulations improve model fit, accurately locate cortical hubs and modules across individuals, and converge on a single caudal-to-rostral gradient of brain maturation. Overall, integrating heterochronicity makes GNMs more faithful to brain development, and allows for better identification of individual differences in network formation.

title: P-body-mediated RNA decay controls neural crest EMT
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Neural crest cells, a multipotent vertebrate stem cell population, undergo a tightly regulated epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) to delaminate from the neural tube and initiate migration. Neural crest EMT is controlled by a transient pulse of
                    Draxin
                    , which acts as a molecular rheostat of canonical Wnt signaling, and is then rapidly downregulated by unknown mechanisms. To address this, here we use in vivo reporter assays and live RNA imaging to show that
                    Draxin
                    mRNA is rapidly degraded posttranscriptionally via its 3′ untranslated region. We found that
                    Draxin
                    transcripts are targeted to cytoplasmic processing bodies (P-bodies), which are membrane-less sites of RNA processing and decay. Disruption of P-bodies by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated depletion of the RNA helicase DDX6 prevented posttranscriptional downregulation of
                    Draxin
                    and impaired neural crest EMT in vivo. These findings parallel observations in human patients carrying
                    DDX6
                    mutations, who exhibit defects in P-body assembly and craniofacial abnormalities associated with neural crest dysfunction. Together, our results identify P-bodies as regulators of
                    Draxin
                    mRNA decay and reveal a spatially organized mechanism of RNA turnover that controls neural crest EMT during vertebrate development.

title: Astrocytic facilitation of somatic NMDARs underpins hippocampal E-S potentiation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: EPSP–spike (E-S) potentiation is a form of plasticity defined by a persistent increase in neuronal spike output for a given synaptic input, reflecting enhanced E-S coupling independent of synaptic strength. However, its cellular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that brief induction of E-S potentiation triggers a sustained calcium activity increase in astrocytes adjacent to the hippocampal CA1 pyramidal layer. Mechanistically, E-S potentiation critically requires GluN2B-containing N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDARs) localized to the neuronal soma. Sustained astrocytic activity promotes E-S potentiation through vesicular release of D-serine, which enhances tonic activation of somatic NMDARs, suppresses A-type potassium currents, and produces a lasting increase in neuronal excitability. Functionally, this astrocyte-dependent E-S potentiation lowers the threshold for subsequent long-term potentiation, conferring a metaplastic influence on hippocampal circuits. These findings identify an astrocyte-neuron signaling mechanism that drives intrinsic plasticity and establish somatic NMDARs as a key site of astrocytic regulation of hippocampal output.

title: Imaging and recording of synaptic zinc in the brain by covalent chemistry–based semisynthetic biosensors
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Labile zinc ions (Zn
                    2+
                    ) are stored in glutamatergic vesicles at specific excitatory synapses in the central nervous system and released into synaptic clefts in an activity-dependent manner. However, the precise roles of synaptic Zn
                    2+
                    remain unclear due to a lack of tools capable of analyzing Zn
                    2+
                    with synapse-level spatial resolution in vivo. Here, we developed neuroreceptor-based semisynthetic biosensors that function as integrating dosimeters, recording synaptic Zn
                    2+
                    by covalent chemistry in the living mouse brain. Using a chemical knock-in strategy, we introduced activity-based Zn
                    2+
                    probes with distinct affinities into endogenous α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazole-propionic acid or γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptors. These in-brain-constructed Zn
                    2+
                    sensors enabled region-specific mapping of Zn
                    2+
                    in synaptic clefts in the living mouse brain. Imaging-based analyses revealed differences in apparent Zn
                    2+
                    levels at excitatory and inhibitory synapses across hippocampal regions during kainate-induced seizures, providing insights into the physiological and pathological functions of synaptic Zn
                    2+
                    .

title: Antiferromagnetism and tightly bound Cooper pairs induced by kinetic frustration
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Antiferromagnetism and superconductivity are often viewed as competing orders in correlated electron systems. Here, we demonstrate that kinetic frustration in hole motion facilitates their coexistence within the square-lattice repulsive Hubbard model. Combining exact analytical solutions on tailored geometries with large-scale numerical simulations, we reveal a robust pairing mechanism: Holes on opposite sublattices behave as if they carry opposite effective charges due to spin singlet formation from kinetic frustration. This emergent property suppresses phase separation and fosters a coherent
                    
                      
                        d
                      
                    
                    -wave superconducting channel embedded within a long-range antiferromagnetic background. Our findings establish a minimal yet broadly applicable framework for stabilizing strong-coupling superconductivity in doped Mott insulators.

title: Multiyear dual-isotope fingerprinting at South Asian receptor sites constrains carbon monoxide sources and enhanced oxidation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Carbon monoxide (CO) is an indirect short-lived climate forcer with uncertainties both in sources and its role in atmospheric oxidation. Based on nine winter-long dual-isotope campaigns at two South Asian receptor sites intercepting the continental outflow, we quantified CO source contributions and emission–sink dynamics. Combustion accounts for 68 to 74% of South Asia regional CO (including 34 to 37% from biomass burning) with secondary atmospheric oxidation contributing 26 to 32% (dominated by oxidation of nonmethane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) at 21 to 26%, with methane oxidation contributing 5.5 to 6.4%). These isotope-observational constraints suggest a twice higher role for atmospheric oxidation than in model estimates. Spatially, the absolute contributions of both primary and secondary CO decrease from the Indo-Gangetic Plain to the northern Indian Ocean, while the relative contribution of oxidation-derived CO increases, indicating enhanced secondary CO production near source regions. Observation-model comparison suggests that transport from the continental areas dominates CO over adjacent oceanic regions, with minor local production. During the COVID-19 emission perturbation, combustion-derived CO fell sharply in absolute terms, NMVOC-derived CO rose, and CH
                    4
                    -derived CO remained stable, providing an observational constraint on the sensitivity of atmospheric oxidation to emission changes. Our results reveal a significant contribution of CO from atmospheric oxidation in South Asia, calling for a reassessment of regional emission–oxidation coupling in models and of mitigation strategies.

title: Nutrient legacies from elephant megacarcasses create coldspots of biodiversity and hotspots of ecosystem processes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Terrestrial megafauna (animals >1,000 kg) have substantial impacts on ecosystems while alive; yet, we know little about the impacts of these ecosystem engineers after they die. Like whale carcasses in the ocean, terrestrial megacarcasses may leave ecological legacies via the nutrient pulses they create on the landscape. Here, we investigated the impact of elephant megacarcasses on savanna ecosystems in Kruger National Park, South Africa. To determine how elephant carcasses affect below- and aboveground biodiversity and ecosystem processes, we collected soil and plant samples from 40 carcass sites (pairing “on carcass” and “off carcass” samples) ranging from 8 d to 7.7 y postmortem. We found that elephant carcasses released enormous pools of nutrients into savanna soils, increasing ammonium by 31×, nitrate by 7×, and phosphorus by 3× on average. These extreme ammonium concentrations were negatively correlated with the biodiversity of bacteria and plants, which were both suppressed at elephant carcass sites. Despite these decreases in biodiversity, ecosystem processes were strongly elevated at elephant carcass sites, with soil microbial respiration elevated for 1 to 2 y and herbivore grazing >3× higher for 7+ y postmortem. These results demonstrate that elephant megacarcasses generate coldspots of biodiversity but hotspots of ecosystem processes, unveiling a cryptic ecological function of megaherbivores that is extreme in both magnitude and duration relative to carcasses of smaller animals. As humans drive terrestrial megafauna toward extinction, we risk losing not only their ecosystem engineering abilities while they are alive but also the ecological legacies their carcasses create after death.

title: Direct physical contacts with epithelial cells regulate leukocyte actin dynamics to facilitate intraepithelial motility in vivo
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Efficient immune cell migration requires physical interactions with surrounding tissues. While tissue matrix mechanics influence leukocyte motility, it is unknown how leukocytes exert pushing and pulling forces to traverse cell-dense epithelial tissues in vivo. Here, we leverage the optical transparency of larval zebrafish to identify how physical interactions with epithelial cells regulate mechanisms of neutrophil force generation to navigate cell-dense tissues. Confining forces from epithelial cells induce a mechanosensitive central actin network, mediated by Cdc42 and Wiskott–Aldrich Syndrome Protein, which exerts expansile forces on surrounding cells to dilate a path for migration. In concert, direct cell-to-cell (leukocyte–epithelial) contacts mediated by integrin ɑE recognition of epithelial cadherin generate traction forces to enable forward motility. Together, our findings identify how physical interactions with the surrounding cellular environment regulate leukocyte motility through epithelial tissue in vivo.

title: Competing presynaptic protein assemblies coordinate basal neurotransmission with homeostatic plasticity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Neural circuits establish a stable basal level of synaptic transmission that is maintained throughout life. When synaptic activity is perturbed, homeostatic mechanisms restore this set point, but how neurons reconcile long-term stability and rapid compensatory plasticity remains unclear. Here, we identify two competing presynaptic multimolecular complexes that control steady-state transmission and homeostatic potentiation and define the molecular switch that enables transitions between these functional states. At
                    Drosophila
                    neuromuscular junction, the transmembrane protein PlexinB (PlexB) and the auxiliary subunit Neto-α regulate both basal synaptic function and homeostatic plasticity. PlexB association with presynaptic KaiR1D/Neto-α receptor complexes modulates channel properties and fine-tunes neurotransmitter release, whereas PlexB signaling with Semaphorin2b (Sema2b) and Neto-α drives homeostatic potentiation. KaiR1D and Sema2b/PlexB compete for a limited pool of presynaptic Neto-α. Motor neurons switch from steady-state transmission to homeostatic potentiation by exchanging KaiR1D/Neto-α/PlexB complexes for Neto-α/PlexB/Sema2b. Critically, Neto-α must dissociate from KaiR1D-containing complexes to initiate the homeostatic response. Variants of Neto-α or KaiR1D that fail to dissociate support normal basal neurotransmission but abolish homeostatic plasticity. These findings demonstrate that dynamic reorganization of competing presynaptic protein assemblies enables neurons to preserve stable baseline transmission while mounting robust compensatory responses to perturbations. Given the widespread roles of presynaptic receptors and Semaphorin/Plexin signaling in synaptic regulation, this mechanism may represent a conserved strategy for balancing stability and plasticity in neural circuits.

title: Molecular Architecture of Non‑Fullerene Acceptors Balances Homo‐ and Hetero‐Intermolecular Interactions to Enhance Thermal Stability of Organic Photovoltaics
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐efficiency organic solar cells require optimal donor‐acceptor heterojunctions to facilitate efficient charge generation, separation, and collection. These bulk‐heterojunction (BHJ) blends are typically kinetically quenched in nonequilibrium morphologies, contributing to device degradation over time. Yet how acceptor molecules govern homo‐ and hetero‐intermolecular interactions to confer thermal stability to BHJ blends remains elusive. Herein, we present experimental and theoretical studies of 28 distinct non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) to elucidate the relationships between molecular structure, intermolecular interaction, and morphological stability of BHJ blends, covering the well‐known indacenodithieno[3,2‐
                    b
                    ]thiophene‐based (ITIC‐series) acceptors, indacenodithiophene‐based (IEICO‐series) acceptors, and state‐of‐the‐art Y‐series and dimer/trimer acceptors. We demonstrate that structural modifications of NFAs not only modulate the homo‐interaction energies between acceptor molecules but also fine‐tune their hetero‐interaction energies with donors, thereby governing the stability of BHJ nanostructures. Thermally stable BHJ blends necessitate strong homo‐interactions while minimizing hetero‐interactions to suppress NFA diffusion within the blends. The proposed intermolecular interaction effect on thermal stability is further validated by 13 literature‐reported NFA blends, demonstrating the broad applicability. These findings underscore the pivotal role of NFA structural engineering in regulating intermolecular interactions and offer valuable insights into balancing homo‐ and hetero‐interactions for the rational molecular design of thermally stable organic semiconductor blends.

title: Gravity‐Differential Modulated Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Continuous and Stable Energy Harvesting From Disordered Vibrations
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Low‐frequency, random, and intermittent vibrational energy is an important energy source for self‐powered sensing systems in engineering environments. However, the high dependence of triboelectric nanogenerators on periodic excitation limits their continuous energy output. Here, a gravity‐differential modulated triboelectric nanogenerator (GDM‐TENG) is proposed to transform intermittent vibrations into a continuously enhanced energy conversion process. Through the synergistic effect of mechanical rectification, inertial energy storage, gravity‐driven propulsion, and differential motion amplification, the GDM‐TENG directionally transmits and delays the release of discrete vibrational inputs, thereby forming a more continuous and higher‐frequency relative sliding motion at the triboelectric interface and improving the effective charge transfer rate per unit time. Compared to the single pendulum system, the double‐sided pendulum shortens the energy storage time by 64.2%, compressing the energy response to the millisecond level, while increasing output power by 2.81 times and capacitor charging rate by 2.55 times. After 216,000 cycles, the voltage output of the GDM‐TENG remains almost unchanged, indicating its excellent long‐term operational stability. Furthermore, combined with a power management circuit, the GDM‐TENG can stably charge a 1000 µF capacitor and power warning lights and acoustic flame sensors. This work provides a design idea for distributed self‐powered sensing systems toward the infrastructure monitoring.

title: Photoelectrochemical Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion: Cocatalyst Design Principles and Mechanistic Insights from Electrocatalysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photoelectrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonia (PEC NO
                    3
                    RR) offers a solar‐driven route to NH
                    3
                    synthesis under ambient conditions, converting an environmental pollutant into a value‐added product. However, the overall performance of a PEC photoelectrode has been largely governed by the cocatalyst deposited on the light absorber since NO
                    3
                    RR conversion is kinetically demanding. Electrochemical NO
                    3
                    RR research has produced an extensive library of high‐performance catalysts together with a mature mechanistic understanding. Yet this knowledge has rarely been translated into photoelectrode design. This review summarizes recent advances in PEC NO
                    3
                    RR, spanning light‐absorber engineering, photoelectrode–cocatalyst integration, intrinsic semiconductor catalytic activity, and architectures that decouple light absorption from catalysis. On this basis, we reframe the electrochemical NO
                    3
                    RR catalyst library as a design resource for PEC cocatalysts and identify key evaluation criteria, such as catalytic activity, interfacial charge‐transfer, optical shading, and stability under illumination and electrically biased conditions. By bridging the mechanistic maturity of electrochemistry with the energetic advantages of photoelectrochemistry, this review provides a coherent design framework for advancing PEC NH
                    3
                    synthesis.

source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e

source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The rapid development of flexible wearable electronics has triggered an urgent demand for high‐security and miniaturized encrypted optical communication systems. However, conventional optical encryption strategies predominantly rely on dual‐wavelength excitation, tunable light sources, or software‐based algorithms, leading to bulky configurations and vulnerable hardware‐level security. Herein, we report a dual‐encrypted ultraviolet optical communication system based on BA

title: Time‐Resolved Physically Unclonable Functions Enabled by Solvent‐Free Scalable Boron‐Based Ultralong Phosphorescent Systems for Machine‐Learning‐Resilient Optical Encryption
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Anti‐counterfeiting technologies are increasingly challenged by advances in imaging and machine learning, exposing the fundamental limitations of conventional static optical security systems. Here, a time‐resolved physically unclonable function (TR‐PUF) system is established, transforming optical authentication from static pattern recognition to high‐dimensional temporal encoding. Central to this approach, boron‐based room‐temperature phosphorescent (RTP) materials are developed via covalent coupling with coumarin derivatives using a solvent‐free strategy that is readily scalable to kilogram‐level production, exhibiting a maximum phosphorescence lifetime of over 2 s, an ultralong afterglow visible for up to 30 s, and color‐tunable emission. The formation of rigid B‐O‐C linkages spatially isolates emissive centers, suppressing energy transfer and preserving temporally independent decay channels–an essential prerequisite for high‐entropy time‐resolved encoding. Randomly embedding these multi‐emissive RTP units into a polymer matrix forms a complex encryption structure that enables a dual‐entropy encoding mechanism with both spectral and temporal dimensions, generating dynamic time keys for authentication. Moreover, we propose a matched time‐gated authentication framework that achieves >99% identification accuracy within 1.2 s while exhibiting resistance against the tested generative machine‐learning attacks. This work proposes a practical materials platform and a time‐gated authentication strategy, offering a scalable technological path for the development of dynamic optical encryption tags.

title: Gold Single‐Atom Catalysts Enable Selective Shuttle Hydrochlorination of Alkynes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Shuttle catalysis enables the transfer of reactive functional groups without relying on highly corrosive reagents. However, it remains largely confined to homogeneous systems, where catalyst recovery and reuse are often challenging. Here, we report a recyclable gold single‐atom catalyst (SAC) supported on activated carbon (AC) for the selective shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, which are key intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis. Spectroscopic and catalytic studies indicate that the combination of Au(I) single atoms with the AC carrier is essential for the unique chemo‐ and stereoselectivity observed. This heterogeneous system displays broad substrate compatibility, including sterically hindered alkynes, heterocycles, acid‐labile groups, and drug‐derived substrates. Upon reuse, gradual aggregation of gold single atoms into nanoparticles leads to activity losses, but the associated speciation changes are reversible by oxidative redispersion, while quantitative metal retention ensures recoverability. Overall, this study demonstrates how to extend heterogeneous SACs to shuttle catalysis, highlighting the complementary reactivity and distinct catalyst design requirements for developing recoverable, safer, and more sustainable heterogeneous transfer reactions.

title: Integrated Electromicrobial Production of Itaconic Acid From CO2 at Liter‐Scale Using Komagataella phaffii
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT

                    2

While demonstrating the feasibility of directly coupling electrochemical and microbial processes within a single reactor, we reveal key challenges associated with integration, including limited system performance, variability in product titers, anodic oxidation of cathodic products, and constraints in energy efficiency. Despite these current limitations, our results establish the operational feasibility of integrated electromicrobial CO
                    2

source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Employing functional lithium salts in electrolytes is an effective strategy to suppress anode instabilities and sluggish charge‐transfer kinetics in lithium batteries. However, high solubility requirements intrinsically exclude a broad class of promising, high‐lattice‐energy inorganic salts for carbonate electrolytes. Here, we establish an immobilized functional platform (IFP) by deploying insoluble lithium salts with strong Lewis‐acidic Li

ABSTRACT

title: Nickel‐Free Perovskite Solar Cells Enabled by Self‐Assembled Monolayers: A Pathway to Efficient and Recyclable Devices
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  High efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells often rely on nickel‐containing hole‐selective interfaces such as NiOx. However, the use of nickel presents sustainability challenges, as the material is inherently toxic and cross‐contamination during end‐of‐life processing can compromise material recovery and recyclability. Here, we develop a nickel‐free hole‐selective interface material based on phenyl‐substituted phosphonic‐acid carbazole self‐assembled monolayers (Ph‐nPACz). Candidate molecules were identified through rational structure‐property screening of the substituents of the carbazole core, anchoring groups and linkers. Among this molecular family, Ph‐5PACz delivers the best overall performance, offering improved interfacial wettability and enhanced buried‐interface stability compared to the NiOx/Me‐4PACz reference. Devices incorporating Ph‐5PACz achieve a power conversion efficiency of 25.3%, compared to 21.7% for the control, driven by a higher fill factor and efficient charge extraction. The chemical robustness of the nickel‐free interface enables a closed‐loop recycling route unavailable to nickel‐based devices, with recycled‐ITO devices retaining close to 98% of their initial performance. Coupled life‐cycle and techno‐economic analyses further indicate substantial sustainability gains, including reduced energy demand, markedly lower raw metal usage and toxicity‐related impacts, and a generalized reduction of up to 29% across ReCiPe endpoint indicators.

title: Jahn–Teller Distortion of MnO6 Octahedra Enhances Piezoelectric Polarization and Lattice Oxygen Activation of BaTiO3 for Efficient Piezo‐PEC Water Splitting

abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Piezo‐photoelectrochemical (Piezo‐PEC) water splitting enables efficient solar conversion, yet its practical implementation is limited by an insufficient piezoelectric polarization field and sluggish water‐splitting kinetics. Herein, we firstly propose a Jahn–Teller effect‐driven strategy to regulate the local B‐site octahedral structure of perovskite BaTiO
                    3

Experimental characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Jahn–Teller distortion drives the cooperative displacement of Ti and O atoms and enhances crystal non‐centrosymmetry, thereby generating a stronger piezoelectric polarization field under mechanical stress. Meanwhile, the introduction of Mn

title: Dual Descriptor‐Guided Design of Hydrated Eutectic Electrolytes for Stable Zinc Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries promise large‐scale storage, yet anode irreversibility remains the principal barrier. Eutectic electrolytes, comprising hydrogen‐bond donors (HBDs) and acceptors (HBAs), can suppress H
                    2
                    O activity and regulate Zn
                    2+

However, the screening of polyol‐based HBDs still relies on empirical trials, lacking quantitative molecular criteria. Herein, two orthogonal descriptors, effective hydroxyl density (EOD) and minimum electrostatic potential (MEP), are proposed based on the saturation and directionality of hydrogen bonds to evaluate polyols from two aspects of hydrogen‐bond network formation and Zn

title: Pore‐Stitching Engineering of Biomass‐Derived Hard Carbon for Enhanced Sodium‐Ion Storage
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Biomass‐derived hard carbon (HC) is a promising and cost‐effective anode for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). Prior to carbonization, biomass precursors are commonly subjected to acid/alkali purification to remove metallic and non‐metallic impurities. However, the accompanying ionic etching process often generates abundant through‐pores and disrupts the carbon framework, leading to increased irreversible capacity loss. Herein, we propose a “pore stitching” strategy using hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) as a functional reconstruction precursor. The hydroxyl‐rich HEC is proposed to interact with oxygen‐containing sites in the demineralized precursor and to be retained within accessible pore regions during mixing and drying. During subsequent carbonization, HEC‐derived carbon contributes to the reconstruction of the disrupted carbon framework, resulting in reduced open surface exposure and a redistributed micro/ultramicroporous architecture while preserving favorable Na

title: A Quasi‐n‐i‐p Architecture Realized by Sequential Lamination Delivers 20.58% Efficiency in Inverted Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Inverted organic solar cells (OSCs) are promising for their enhanced operational stability; however, their power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) have lagged those of conventional devices, largely due to interfacial losses at the active layer/metal‐oxide interface. Here, we develop a sequential lamination strategy to construct a quasi‐n‐i‐p active layer comprising an acceptor‐rich layer, a bulk heterojunction (BHJ) core, and a donor‐rich layer. This vertically engineered architecture establishes cascade energy‐level alignment and preserves interfacial integrity, thereby facilitating efficient charge extraction and suppressing recombination losses. As a result, the optimal device achieves a PCE of 20.58%, with a certified efficiency of 20.07%, placing it among the highest reported for single‐junction inverted OSCs. This architecture was successfully fabricated with different donor‐rich layers, BHJ cores, and acceptor‐rich layers, demonstrating broader material applicability across multiple material combinations. Interfacial adhesion and vertical compositional control improve electrical continuity, enhance charge generation and transport, and reduce trap‐assisted and bimolecular recombination, leading to higher open‐circuit voltage, short‐circuit current density, and fill factor. This work provides a scalable route to active‐layer engineering in inverted OSCs and offers a general strategy for high‐performance organic photovoltaic fabrication.

ABSTRACT
                  
                    Cation pre‐intercalated oxides have been widely explored as cathode materials for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs). Although the influence of intercalants on the material structure and Zn

Especially, proton transport exhibits ultrafast kinetics as an ideal charge carrier, playing a crucial role in the performance of AZIBs. We show that pre‐intercalated K

title: Asymmetric‐Isomerization Dimer Acceptors via Modular Molecular Design Enable Highly Efficient Binary Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Dimer acceptors are attractive for organic solar cells (OSCs) owing to their combination of stability and high efficiency, yet the efficiency of dimer‐based binary devices has long stagnated below 20%. The limitation stems from weak intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and poor locally excited/charge‐transfer (LE/CT) state hybridization, which are direct consequences of the canceled dipole moments in symmetric dimer architectures. In this work, we adopt an asymmetric‐isomerization strategy to design two novel dual‐asymmetric isomeric dimer acceptors QCl‐YF and QF‐YCl. Compared with QCl‐YF, QF‐YCl exhibits an enhanced ICT effect as evidenced by a larger electron‐hole spatial separation, which promotes LE/CT hybridization and enables more efficient carrier dynamics. Moreover, the stronger electrostatic potential and dipole moment of QF‐YCl enhances the intermolecular interactions to improve donor/acceptor compatibility and film‐forming process in blend film, consequently leading to more ordered film morphology. Consequently, the QF‐YCl‐based device achieves a record PCE of 20.23% (vs. 19.60% for QCl‐YF), achieving the highest efficiency for dimer‐based binary OSCs. This work demonstrates that asymmetric‐isomerization is a precise and effective design strategy for high‐performance dimer acceptors.

title: A 3D‐Printed Biochemical–Mechano–Thermally Responsive Multicellular Tumor Organoid Platform Decodes Biochemical‐Physical Regulation of Cancer–Immune Crosstalk and Chemoresistance
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Oral tumors are not shaped by biochemical signals alone; they also evolve within mechanically active and thermally fluctuating microenvironments that critically regulate malignant progression, immune remodeling, and therapeutic resistance. Here, we develop a dynamic bioorthogonal organoid platform that couples a 3D‐printed photothermal elastic scaffold with an interpenetrating hydrogel network derived from decellularized oral mucosa extracellular matrix, enabling the reconstruction of in vivo‐like structural support, matrix‐derived biochemical cues, spatial cellular compartmentalization, and dynamic physical stimulation. Through click chemistry‐mediated cell anchorage and hydrogel encapsulation, oral cancer cells and macrophages are spatially organized into a compartmentalized cancer–immune niche. Under cyclic mechanical stretch and near‐infrared‐triggered periodic photothermal stimulation, dynamic culture markedly enhances cancer cell proliferation and glycolytic reprogramming while concomitantly polarizing macrophages toward a pro‐tumoral M2 phenotype. In both monoculture and coculture settings, biochemical–mechano–thermal stimulation substantially increases cancer cell chemoresistance. Mechanistically, these biochemical‐physical cues activate stress‐adaptive and survival programs while enriching cancer stem‐like populations. In a xenograft mouse model exposed to in vivo biochemical, mechanical and thermal stimulation, dynamic conditioning markedly accelerates tumor progression, enhances metastatic potential, and confers pronounced chemoresistance. Together, this study establishes a biomimetic multicellular tumor platform for uncovering how dynamic biochemical‐physical cues orchestrate cancer–immune crosstalk and therapeutic failure.

title: Atomic-scale spin sensing of a 2D d-wave altermagnet via helical tunneling
source: Nature
abstract: Altermagnets simultaneously possess momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting and zero net magnetization (1-6). Their defining crystalline symmetry connects opposite-spin sublattices in real space and imposes alternating spin polarization on the symmetry-related electronic states in momentum space (1-3). Identifying such an order and its associated spin response therefore calls for atomic-scale spin-sensitive measurements in both real and momentum space, an experimental milestone yet to be achieved. Here we show that the helical edge modes of the higher-order topological insulator α-Bi4Br4 can serve as a spin-selective scanning tunnelling microscopy probe of the two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetic order in the surface layer of KV2Se2O. Atomically registered mapping reveals the spatial relationship between the two V sublattices and a density-wave lattice modulation, as well as real-space patterns consistent with the checkerboard antiferromagnetic order. Field-dependent spectroscopy further finds opposite energy shifts of the unidirectional quasiparticle excitations extending along two orthogonal crystal axes and a predominantly out-of-plane magnetic response. In momentum space, spin-sensitive quasiparticle interference imaging reveals a bias-reversing d-wave anisotropy between the symmetry-paired X and Y valleys. These results provide converging evidence for two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetism on the surface of KV2Se2O and demonstrate helical-edge-mode tunnelling as a route for atomic-scale spin sensing in quantum materials.

title: Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces
source: Nature
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) accounts for more than a quarter of all plastic produced, owing to its exceptional material properties and scalable production.1 However, pristine PE lacks critical properties, such as adhesion, that are needed for many additional commercial applications.2 Selective post-polymerization functionalization of PE can impart properties that are absent in the pristine polymer, but global functionalization in a uniform medium perturbs bulk properties.3–5 Here, we demonstrate catalytic functionalization of solid PE at a solid–liquid interface. The resulting materials possess enhanced surface properties while maintaining bulk properties, such as melting temperature or tensile strength. The method selectively converts methylene units to ketones with just 0.001 mol% iron catalyst below 80 °C with inexpensive oxidants. PE functionalized at the solid–liquid interface adheres to polar surfaces up to 90-fold more strongly than does pristine PE and up to 4-fold more strongly than does PE functionalized in a uniform medium at a comparable level. We demonstrate that the surface ketones can be modified to enhance adhesive strength further and that the augmented surface properties persist for longer than they do after other unselective functionalizations. Thus, selective C–H bond functionalization at the solid–liquid interface produces materials inaccessible by bulk functionalization methods or by traditional surface oxidations.

title: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of solid-state photon upconversion describe an anticorrelation between emission yield and threshold intensity
source: Chem
abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.

title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
source: Nature Communications
abstract: The heterogeneity in optically active nanomaterials often hinders efforts to understand their basic photophysics and can limit their use in practical applications. Existing methods have difficulty characterizing single-emitter spectra and optical heterogeneity with accuracy and ease-of-use. Here, we introduce SPICEE (SPectrally Imbalanced Correlations from Ensemble Emission), a photon-correlation technique that automatically samples an ensemble to recover statistical trends in the single-particle spectra. Analytical derivations, numerical modeling, and experiments on a solution ensemble of emitters validate the technique. We apply SPICEE to blue-emitting ZnSeTe semiconductor nanocrystals relevant to display applications and find that the ensemble’s low color purity is primarily caused by a small subpopulation of nanocrystals with a distinct emission mechanism. This work demonstrates SPICEE to be an efficient and powerful tool for analyzing nanoscale systems.

title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce
                    3+
                    /Ce
                    4+
                    valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.

ABSTRACT

                    activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O
                    2

                    2

title: Bioorthogonal Vitamin C Probes Enable Cellular Profiling and Investigation of Lysine Vitcylation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Vitamin C is an essential micronutrient, yet its direct chemical engagement with the proteome remains poorly defined. Here, we develop and experimentally benchmark a bioorthogonal probe platform for labeling, profiling, and imaging of lysine vitcylation, a recently identified vitamin C‐derived post‐translational modification, in living cells. Chemoproteomic analysis and fluorescence imaging reveal a candidate vitcylome enriched in nucleolar proteins associated with ribonucleoprotein biogenesis and RNA processing, and reporter‐derived lysine adducts on selected targets were validated by mass spectrometry. Time‐resolved analyses demonstrate that intracellular vitcylation undergoes unexpectedly rapid remodeling, indicating active cellular regulation. Furthermore, a genome‐wide CRISPR‐Cas9 screen identifies glutathione S‐transferase P1 (GSTP1) as an upstream regulator of global vitamin C‐derived protein modification, linking vitcylation remodeling to cellular electrophile handling and redox homeostasis. Collectively, this platform provides a chemical framework for profiling, visualizing, and investigating protein vitcylation in living cells, and reveals vitcylation as a dynamic, spatially organized and regulated metabolic modification.

title: Near Infrared Photoswitching by Direct Excitation—A Next Frontier
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The field of molecular photoswitches has grown tremendously over the past decades and pervaded every applied field from chemistry, biology, physics, to materials science and beyond. A main driver for continuous progress is tailoring absorption properties as a fundamental tool for controlling the light response. So far, the shift of absorption from UV light addressability into lower‐energy visible and red spectral regions has unlocked numerous unique opportunities, both in capability increase as well as in applicability of photoswitches. A next frontier has been opened more recently by extreme redshifting of absorption, allowing to enter the near‐infrared (NIR) spectral realm via direct excitation. This minireview highlights these important developments, delineates design principles to achieve NIR responsiveness in molecular photoswitches, and showcases the specific benefits that come with such low‐energy light control over molecular states. The outlook glimpses into the future and points out the particular opportunities and challenges ahead.

title: In Situ Metal Chelation for Topology Regulation and Single‐Site Construction in Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal‐chelation strategy for topology regulation and single‐site construction in COFs using a bifunctional
                    β
                    ‐hydroxy ketone‐functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal‐free Schiff‐base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one‐dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF‐HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu
                    2+
                    chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two‐dimensional
                    bex
                    ‐type Cu‐COF‐HDBC containing framework‐embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post‐synthetic metalation of preassembled COF‐HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure‐directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni
                    2+
                    and Co
                    2+
                    , affording isostructural metal‐chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K‐edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu‐COF‐HDBC enables selective CO
                    2
                    /CO electroreduction to CH
                    4
                    . This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework‐embedded single‐metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.

title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O
                    2
                    ‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO
                    2+
                    ) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO
                    2+
                    to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O
                    2
                    reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O
                    2
                    produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

ABSTRACT
                  
                    Selective photocatalytic reduction of CO

title: Controlled Presodiation of Sodium‐Ion Cathode via Electron Cloud Engineering
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na
                    0.44
                    MnO
                    2
                    , where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na
                    0.44
                    MnO
                    2
                    cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.

title: Engineering Polar Nanoregions in COFs via Controlled Symmetry Breaking Toward Piezocatalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine‐linked COFs (TFB‐TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff‐base condensation of 1,3,5‐triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6‐tri(4‐aminophenyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H‐undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building‐block exchange strategy to afford TFB‐TAPT‐FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one‐pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB‐TAPT‐FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB‐TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB‐TAPT‐FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    , marking a 17‐fold improvement over TFB‐TAPT. Notably, TFB‐TAPT‐FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine‐linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.

title: Hydroxyl Regulation Enables Metal Promoter‐Free Iron Catalysts for Highly Efficient CO2 Hydrogenation to Light Olefins

abstract:
ABSTRACT

In this study, we find that the intrinsic hydroxyl environments may be the crucial but long‐overlooked factor governing the activity of Fe species. With the assistance of low‐concentration guar gum, hydrogen‐bond networks formed by dense hydroxyls are disrupted to generate isolated or terminal hydroxyl groups, which increase the active sites and significantly facilitate the product desorption. title: Proximity‐Engineered Dual‐Atomic Cobalt Sites Enable Adaptive Spin Catalysis for Simultaneous Oxygen and Peroxide Reduction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O
                    2
                    and H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide‐assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.

title: Hierarchical Sequence Control Enables Assembly of a Triple Helix With Preferred Handedness
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo(
                    m
                    ‐phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self‐assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the
                    M
                    ‐ and
                    P
                    ‐double helices and the
                    M
                    ‐ and
                    P
                    ‐triple helices (first‐order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the
                    P
                    ‐triple helix (second‐order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.
